introduction.q: Which tool turns a .java source file into bytecode?
introduction.explanation: javac is the compiler. The java command runs the compiled bytecode.

introduction.q: What does the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) run?
options: Machine code for one CPU only
introduction.explanation: The compiler produces bytecode in .class files and the JVM runs it, which is why Java programs run on many systems.

introduction.q: Which method is the starting point of a Java program?
introduction.explanation: The JVM looks for exactly this signature to start the program.

introduction.q: Complete the line so it prints Hello and moves to a new line.
introduction.explanation: println prints the text and then starts a new line.
main must be static so the JVM can call it without creating an object.

variables-and-data-types.q: Which data type stores only true or false?

variables-and-data-types.explanation: Both operands are int, so the division is integer division and the decimal part is dropped.
Names cannot start with a digit, a char needs single quotes, and a boolean cannot hold 1.

variables-and-data-types.q: Choose the type for a decimal number.
variables-and-data-types.explanation: 9.99 is a double literal. A float would need the suffix f.
Text is stored in a String. Java is case-sensitive, so it is String with a capital S.

operators.explanation: % gives the remainder: 10 divided by 3 is 3 with remainder 1.
Evaluation goes left to right: 5 + 3 is 8, then the String joins the rest as text: 8x53.
&& is true only when both conditions are true.

operators.q: Add 5 to x using a compound assignment operator.
Both conditions must be true. Fill in the operator.
operators.explanation: && (logical AND) is true only if both sides are true.

input-output.q: Which class is used to read what the user types on the keyboard?
input-output.explanation: Scanner (from java.util) reads input from System.in.

input-output.q: Which Scanner method reads a whole line of text?
input-output.explanation: nextLine() reads up to the end of the line. next() reads one word.
print() does not add a space or a new line.

input-output.q: Create a Scanner that reads from the keyboard.
input-output.explanation: System.in is the keyboard input stream.

input-output.code:
Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
int age = sc.___();
input-output.explanation: nextInt() reads the next whole number.

conditions.explanation: 15 > 10 is true, so only the first branch runs.

conditions.q: What is printed? (Hint: look for break.)
conditions.explanation: case 2 has no break, so execution falls through into case 3, which has a break.

conditions.q: Which condition correctly checks whether x equals 5?
conditions.explanation: == compares values. A single = assigns, and Java needs parentheses and has no ===.
else runs when the if condition is false.

conditions.q: Choose the statement that selects between many cases.
conditions.explanation: switch chooses a case based on one value.

loops.explanation: i starts at 1 and the loop runs while i <= 3.
A do-while checks its condition after the body, so the body runs once even though 10 < 5 is false.

loops.q: Which loop always runs its body at least once?
loops.explanation: do-while tests the condition after running the body.

loops.q: Make the loop count up by one each time.
loops.explanation: i++ adds one to i after every round.

loops.q: Choose the loop that repeats while a condition is true.
loops.explanation: while repeats as long as its condition is true.

arrays.explanation: The last index is length - 1, which is 2, and numbers[2] is 15.

arrays.q: What is the index of the first element of an array?
What happens when this code runs?
arrays.explanation: Valid indexes are 0, 1 and 2. Index 3 is outside the array, which fails at run time.

arrays.q: Create an array of five ints.
arrays.explanation: new int[5] creates an array that holds five ints.
length (no parentheses) is the number of elements in an array.

strings.explanation: charAt(1) returns the character at index 1. Index 0 is H.
Strings are immutable. toUpperCase() returns a new String, and the result was thrown away.

strings.q: Which is the correct way to compare the text of two Strings?
strings.explanation: equals() compares the characters. == compares whether both are the same object.

strings.q: Convert the text to capital letters.
Split the text at each comma.
strings.explanation: split() returns an array of the pieces.

methods.explanation: Java passes a copy of a primitive value, so changing x inside the method does not change n.

methods.q: What does the return type void mean?
methods.explanation: A void method does its work but gives no value back.
n * n is an int, so the method returns int.

methods.q: Choose the return type of a method that returns nothing.

classes-and-objects.q: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
options: An object is a blueprint for classes
A class is a blueprint and an object is one thing made from it
A class is created from an object at run time
classes-and-objects.explanation: A class describes fields and methods. Each object created with new is one instance of it.
c1 and c2 refer to the same Car object, so changing speed through c2 is visible through c1.

classes-and-objects.q: Which line creates a Dog object?
classes-and-objects.explanation: Objects are created with the new keyword and a constructor call.
new allocates the object and calls its constructor.

classes-and-objects.q: Call the method of the object.
classes-and-objects.explanation: Use the dot operator and the method name with parentheses.

constructors.q: Which statement about a constructor is true?
options: It has the same name as the class and no return type
It has any name you like
It is called with the dot operator
constructors.explanation: A constructor shares the class name and has no return type, not even void.
The constructor stores the argument in the title field.

options: A compile-time error, because Book has no constructor without parameters
constructors.explanation: Once you write any constructor, Java no longer provides the default one. new Book() has nothing to call.

constructors.q: Refer to the field of the current object.
constructors.explanation: this.title is the field, title alone is the parameter.
The constructor name must match the class name exactly.

encapsulation.q: Which keyword hides a field so it can only be used inside its own class?
encapsulation.explanation: private limits access to the class itself.

encapsulation.q: Why do we usually put checks inside a setter method?
options: To make the program run faster
To control which values are allowed
Setters are required by the compiler
encapsulation.explanation: A setter can reject invalid values so the object always stays in a valid state.
deposit(-50) is rejected by the check, so only 25 is added.

encapsulation.q: Make the field accessible only inside the class.
encapsulation.explanation: private is the access level that hides a field from other classes.

encapsulation.q: Complete the getter for the balance field.
encapsulation.explanation: By convention a getter is named get followed by the field name.

inheritance.q: Which keyword makes one class inherit from another?
inheritance.explanation: class Dog extends Animal makes Dog a subclass of Animal.
The parent constructor runs first, then the child constructor body.

inheritance.q: Call the parent version of eat().
inheritance.explanation: super refers to the parent class.

polymorphism.explanation: The method that runs depends on the real object (a Dog), not on the variable type.

polymorphism.q: Two methods in the same class have the same name but different parameter lists. What is this called?
polymorphism.explanation: Overloading: same name, different parameters. Overriding: a subclass replaces a parent method.
Java picks the overload whose parameter type matches the argument 5.

polymorphism.q: Mark the method as overriding the parent method.
polymorphism.explanation: @Override asks the compiler to check that you really override a parent method.

polymorphism.q: Store a Dog object in an Animal variable.
polymorphism.explanation: A subclass object can be stored in a variable of its parent type.

abstraction.q: What can you NOT do with an abstract class?
options: Create an object of it with new
abstraction.explanation: An abstract class is incomplete, so it cannot be instantiated directly.

abstraction.q: What does an abstract method look like?
options: It has a body in braces
It has no body and ends with a semicolon
abstraction.explanation: An abstract method only declares the signature. Subclasses provide the body.
area() returns a double, so 3 * 4 prints as 12.0.
abstract marks a class that cannot be instantiated.
An abstract method has no body, so the line ends with a semicolon.

interfaces.q: Which keyword does a class use to follow an interface?
interfaces.explanation: class Card implements Payable promises to provide the interface methods.

interfaces.q: Can one class implement more than one interface?
interfaces.explanation: class A implements X, Y is allowed, unlike extending several classes.
g holds an English object, so greet() from English runs.
implements links a class to an interface.

interfaces.q: Interface methods are public, so the implementation must be too.
interfaces.explanation: Without public the class would try to reduce the visibility, which is a compile error.

exception-handling.explanation: 10 / 0 throws ArithmeticException, the catch block prints Error, and finally always runs.

exception-handling.q: When does a finally block run?
options: Whether or not an exception happens
exception-handling.explanation: finally is for clean-up that must always happen.

exception-handling.q: Which keyword throws an exception yourself?
exception-handling.explanation: throw creates and throws the exception. throws only declares that a method might throw one.
A catch block handles the exception type in parentheses.

exception-handling.q: Signal an invalid argument with the standard exception.
exception-handling.explanation: IllegalArgumentException is the standard choice for a bad argument value.

collections.explanation: remove(0) removes the element at index 0, which is a.
A HashSet ignores duplicates, so the second 2 is not stored.
A map finds a value quickly through its key.
The type on the right of new is the class being created.

collections.q: Add a key and value to the map.
collections.code:
HashMap<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
map.___("Ava", 90);
collections.explanation: put(key, value) stores or replaces an entry.

file-handling.q: Why use try-with-resources when working with files?
file-handling.explanation: Resources declared in the try parentheses are closed automatically, even if an exception occurs.

file-handling.q: Which kind of exception must you handle or declare when reading a file?
file-handling.explanation: IOException is a checked exception, so the compiler forces you to deal with it.
The text written to note.txt is read back by readLine().
FileReader reads characters from a file, and BufferedReader wraps it.
readLine() returns the next line, or null at the end of the file.

jdbc.q: Which call opens a connection to a database?
What is the main benefit of a PreparedStatement with ? placeholders?
options: It removes the need for a driver
jdbc.explanation: Values are sent separately from the SQL text, so user input cannot change the query.
A ResultSet holds the rows returned by a SELECT.
getConnection is the DriverManager method that returns a Connection.

jdbc.q: Move to the next row of the result.
jdbc.explanation: next() moves to the next row and returns false when there are no more rows.
